standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation distinguished triangles and the computation of Ext groups of a truncation
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exact sequence whose last term is Hom_R(H^a(K), M).

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of Ext of a bounded above complex out of an injective module, and the fact that every module embeds in an injective one
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what turns the hypothesis about injective maps into vanishing for all modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion that vanishing of Ext^{-a} against all modules is equivalent to projective amplitude in [a+1, b], and the unique-splitting lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the amplitude bound and then the unique direct sum decomposition.

core_obligations: Consider the truncation distinguished triangle tau_{<= a}K -> K -> tau_{>= a+1}K -> (tau_{<= a}K)[1] in D(R) (proof lines 19928-19934).

Observe that Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = Hom_R(H^a(K), M) and Ext^{-a-1}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = 0, and use the long exact sequence of Ext to obtain the short exact sequence 0 -> Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) -> Ext^{-a}_R(K, M) -> Hom_R(H^a(K), M), functorial in M (proof lines 19935-19947).
Note that for an injective R-module I one has Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, I) = 0 (proof lines 19948-19950).
Since every module injects into an injective module, use the hypothesis on injective maps to conclude that Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) = 0 for every R-module M (proof lines 19951-19952).
Apply the projective-amplitude lemma to conclude that tau_{>= a+1}K has projective-amplitude in [a+1, b] for some b, using that K is bounded above (proof lines 19953-19956).
Obtain the unique direct sum decomposition K = tau_{<= a}K oplus tau_{>= a+1}K from the unique-splitting lemma (proof lines 19956-19957).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an object K of D^-(R), and an integer a, assumes that for every injective R-module map M -> M' the map Ext^{-a}_R(K, M) -> Ext^{-a}_R(K, M') is injective, and concludes that there is a unique direct sum decomposition K = tau_{<= a}K oplus tau_{>= a+1}K with tau_{>= a+1}K of projective-amplitude in [a+1, b] for some b (source lines 19917-19926). The proof starts from the truncation distinguished triangle for K and computes the two Ext groups of tau_{<= a}K: it observes that Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = Hom_R(H^a(K), M) and that Ext^{-a-1}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = 0, so the long exact sequence of Ext yields a short exact sequence 0 -> Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) -> Ext^{-a}_R(K, M) -> Hom_R(H^a(K), M), functorial in M (proof lines 19928-19947). The substantive step is the vanishing: for an injective module I one has Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, I) = 0, and since every module injects into an injective module the hypothesis forces Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) = 0 for every R-module M; the projective-amplitude lemma then gives that tau_{>= a+1}K has projective-amplitude in [a+1, b] for some b, which is where boundedness above is used (proof lines 19948-19956). The splitting then follows from the unique-splitting lemma (proof lines 19956-19957). The non-routine content is the computation of the two Ext groups of the lower truncation and the passage from the vanishing at injective modules to all modules.
